dashboard.scoreExplainer: This score isn't a compliance grade. It reflects how actively and consciously you've dealt with everything on your preventive list — marking something done, planning it, or deliberately skipping it all count as engaging with it. Only items you haven't looked at yet hold the score back.

detail.optedOutScoreNote: A conscious decision like this counts toward your Vorsorge-Score just like a completed item — it won't count against you.
detail.sharedDecisionNote: Worth discussing with your clinician — this is a personal choice, not something you're behind on.

riskProfile.dueDateNote: We'll check back in once this date passes, since this only applies for a limited time.
riskProfile.heading: Tell us more about your health
riskProfile.hematologicMalignancy: I have or have had lymphoma, leukemia, or myeloma
riskProfile.hepatitisB: I was born (or my parents were born) in a region with higher hepatitis B prevalence
riskProfile.highEndemicityHepbOriginOrTr: I was born in, or regularly travel to, a region with higher hepatitis B/A prevalence
riskProfile.highTbIncidenceCountryExposu: I (or my child) have regular exposure to a country with high tuberculosis incidence
riskProfile.hiv: I have a personal risk factor for HIV
riskProfile.immunosuppressiveMedication: I take medication that suppresses my immune system
riskProfile.incarceratedOrCorrectionalSt: I'm currently incarcerated, or work in a correctional facility
riskProfile.infoHepatitisRegionsBody: This generally refers to parts of Africa, South and East Asia, the Pacific, and some regions of Eastern Europe and South America, where hepatitis B is significantly more common than in Central Europe. If you're unsure, it's safer to select this than to leave it out.
riskProfile.infoHepatitisRegionsSource: Illustrative — verify against a source like EviPrev or USPSTF before relying on this.
riskProfile.infoHepatitisRegionsTitle: Regions with higher hepatitis B prevalence
riskProfile.infoTbBody: The WHO maintains a list of high-TB-burden countries, mostly in Africa, South and Southeast Asia, and parts of Eastern Europe.
riskProfile.infoTbSource: Illustrative — verify against a source like EviPrev or USPSTF before relying on this.
riskProfile.infoTbeBody: Tick-borne encephalitis (TBE) mainly occurs in parts of Central and Eastern Europe, plus some regions of Scandinavia and Asia. National health authorities (e.g. BAG, RKI) publish official, annually updated risk-area maps.
riskProfile.infoTbeSource: Illustrative — verify against a source like EviPrev or USPSTF before relying on this.
riskProfile.labPersonnelPathogenExposure: I work in a laboratory with pathogen exposure risk
riskProfile.msm: I'm a man who has sex with men
riskProfile.postpartumUnvaccinated: I recently gave birth and wasn't vaccinated during pregnancy
riskProfile.pretermOrLowBirthweight: My child was born preterm or with low birth weight
riskProfile.pulmonaryChronic: I have a chronic lung condition (e.g. COPD, severe asthma, bronchiectasis)
